title: Restriction compatibility of external section comparisons
statement: Let k be a field [def-weil-field], f:X→Spec(k) and g:Y→Spec(k) schemes [def-pc-scheme], and F,G module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Put M=Gamma(X,F) with its k-action. There is a natural morphism c from the presheaf V↦M tensor_k Gamma(V,G) to the pushforward by pr_2 of the scalar section sheaf of pr_1*F tensor pr_2*G. At the top open it equals the canonical external tensor map [def-sc-scalar-global-sections-comparison]. For every open V of Y there are source and target section isomorphisms identifying c_V with that canonical map for X and the open subscheme V and G restricted to V. No cover or bijectivity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0BED, degree-zero cup product and restriction compatibility

proof.text: For V in Y, restrict the pr_1 pullback of s in Gamma(X,F) to pr_2 inverse-image V, and apply the pr_2 pullback unit to t in G(V). The tensor section of the two is bilinear over k: the scalar structure maps agree by the fibre-product equation. TensorProduct.lift therefore defines c_V. Naturality of the adjunction units and tmulSection_map show that c_V commutes with restrictions, first on pure tensors and then by tensor induction. At the top open, the additional restriction by preimage_top is exactly tensorPullbackTopSection in each factor, proving the normalization equation.

The base change of V→Y identifies X times V with the open pr_2 inverse-image V. On sources, the restriction section iso identifies G restricted to V at top with G(V), preserving the k-action; tensor with Gamma(X,F) to obtain eS. On targets, restrict the external coefficient along this open immersion. Identify restriction with tensor pullback by the open-immersion unit equation, identify pullbacks on the two factors by composition of adjunctions, and identify the pullback of their tensor by the module-pullback-tensor comparison. These give eT on scalar global sections. Each comparison preserves the pulled-back sections by its unit equation. Thus c_V followed by eT equals eS followed by the external tensor comparison over V on pure tensors; tensor induction proves the square for all tensors. Empty opens and zero modules require no exception since all the comparisons are functorial isomorphisms.

theorem exists_externalSectionsRestrictionComparison
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    (F : X.Modules) (G : Y.Modules) :
    ∃ c : scalarPresheaf g G ⋙
        MonoidalCategory.tensorLeft (scalarObj f F (op ⊤)) ⟶
        externalSectionsPushforward f g F G,
      c.app (op ⊤) ≫ (externalSectionsTopIso f g F G).hom =
        ModuleCat.ofHom (externalGlobalSectionsTensor f g F G) ∧
      ∀ V : Y.Opens,
        ∃ eS : (scalarPresheaf g G ⋙
            MonoidalCategory.tensorLeft (scalarObj f F (op ⊤))).obj (op V) ≅
            ModuleCat.of k (scalarObj f F (op ⊤) ⊗[k]
              scalarObj (V.ι ≫ g) (G.restrict V.ι) (op ⊤)),
        ∃ eT : (externalSectionsPushforward f g F G).obj (op V) ≅
            scalarObj (pullback.fst f (V.ι ≫ g) ≫ f)
              (externalCupCoefficients f (V.ι ≫ g) F (G.restrict V.ι)) (op ⊤),
          c.app (op V) ≫ eT.hom = eS.hom ≫
            ModuleCat.ofHom
              (externalGlobalSectionsTensor f (V.ι ≫ g) F (G.restrict V.ι))
